goal: Cross-check the existing interview catalog against Ukrainian and international interview-question banks, deduplicate by concept and interview intent, strengthen source evidence, and add only genuinely missing concepts.

rules: Do not create a new catalog question for wording-only variants.
Theory and scenario questions may remain separate when they test different interview intent.
A source hit strengthens source evidence and prevalence; it does not automatically create another question.
A concept being absent from the current catalog is necessary but not sufficient for adding it: interview value and recurrence must also be considered.
Official documentation validates answer correctness but is not by itself an interview-prevalence signal.
Ukrainian interview banks and international interview banks have equal priority as prevalence evidence.
Broad question banks, interviewer-authored guidance, and fresh market snapshots are tracked separately so one type of source cannot masquerade as another.

batches.label: DOU 250+ and DOU 400+

sources.title: DOU — 400+ QA interview questions for Junior, Middle, Senior

confirmedFindings: DOU 400+ contains internal wording/concept duplicates, so its raw count must never be treated as a unique-question count.
Large parts of DOU 400+ overlap directly with the older DOU 250+ collection, especially Selenium, Web/API, Mobile and practical scenarios.
DOU 400+ also contains additional Git, database, Scrum, behavioural and scenario material that must be checked against the current GimmeJob catalog before being considered new.
DOU 400+ is retained as a first-class Ukrainian-market interview signal rather than being discarded because of overlap.

The DOU 400+ author states that some questions came from interviews and most were collected while reading testing resources; this makes the collection useful as coverage evidence but not proof that every listed question is commonly asked.
observedInternalDuplicateExamples: Smoke vs Sanity appears more than once.
REST API vs SOAP appears more than once.
A/B testing appears more than once.
Database-type and relational-database concepts recur across Web and Database sections.
Emulator vs simulator is split into closely overlapping questions.
Testing without documentation appears in closely overlapping general questions.

batches.label: Other Ukrainian interview sources

sources.title: What questions to ask a QA engineer: a technical interviewer's perspective
sources.authorContext: QA Tech Lead who states she has conducted dozens of Junior-to-Senior QA interviews
sources.value: High Ukrainian-market signal for interview intent: understanding over memorization, case-based reasoning, real tool usage, ambiguity handling and communication. Includes a Top-30 Junior QA topic list.

sources.title: QA tester career guide 2026
sources.value: Very fresh Ukrainian junior-market confirmation. Explicitly lists testing/types, severity vs priority, test case vs checklist, bug report, smoke/regression/sanity and SDLC/STLC as common junior interview prompts. Narrow source, so use as prevalence confirmation rather than a broad bank.

sources.title: DOU VoiceChat: What QA needs to know for interviews
sources.value: Supporting Ukrainian context for Junior/Middle/Senior interview tasks and expectations; not treated as an independent large question bank.

confirmedFindings: Fresh Ukrainian interviewer guidance reinforces classic fundamentals but places more weight on explaining concepts in context than reciting definitions.

Case-based questions such as a production bug, a product without documentation, disagreement with a developer, and ambiguous input are strong local-market signals and should be matched by interview intent, not only keywords.
The August 2026 Mate snapshot independently confirms several classic fundamentals as still current for Junior QA interviews in Ukraine, reducing concern that the DOU fundamentals are obsolete.
